diagrams.title: The Wrap Machine, From Target List to Servicer
diagrams.subtitle: Mirror wrap in, equity wrap out, spread earned on the full balance
diagrams.caption: Five steps practitioners describe for laying a larger wrap note over a live underlying loan, with the buyer paying the wrap holder and a servicer paying the original lender first.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Targeting filters come from Chris Goff's nationwide query; buy-side and sell-side structures come from Bill Brunchick; servicing order comes from Scott Horne. No figures beyond those reported are implied.
diagrams.note: Sources: Chris Goff (X_UODDIMvFs), Bill Brunchick with Kris Haskins (kM__5b36grI), Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network (VDXOvtqzbZk).

stages.label: Pull Absentee-Owner Targets
stages.detail: Chris Goff filters absentee owners with values above $300,000, at least 20% equity and two-plus years of ownership; his nationwide query returned 7,284,401 properties.

stages.label: Buy on a Mirror Wrap
stages.detail: Brunchick buys on a mirror wrap when there is little or no equity, matching the underlying terms.

stages.label: Sell on an Equity Wrap
stages.detail: Mark up both price and rate so the spread runs on the full balance; Brunchick shows 6% on $20,000 of equity plus a 2% gap on an $80,000 first at 4%.

stages.label: Record the Security Instrument
stages.detail: Never record the note itself; record the deed of trust or mortgage with the wraparound rider (Brunchick).

stages.label: Board a Payment Servicer
stages.detail: Scott Horne routes every payment through a servicer that pays the underlying lender first and the seller last, the industry's fraud preventer.

diagrams.title: Due-on-Sale Exposure, From Deal Samples to Cure Clocks
diagrams.subtitle: Reported call counts narrow to the operator's time-boxed controls
diagrams.caption: Practitioner-reported sample sizes and call counts show the clause is a lender right rarely exercised, followed by the two clocks operators manage when it matters.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each stage is a separate practitioner sample or rule, not one cohort; conversions restate each speaker's own reported outcome and are not chained probabilities.
diagrams.note: Sources: Investor Army Podcast guest (WFGzQCgPP54), Horne Real Estate Law (00RujvVfDRc), Pace Morby (cOTyo3LTDPk), In Rem Podcast (d9fjKwIC-VE).

stages.detail: Investor Army Podcast guest's count across owner-financed mortgages.

stages.label: Owner-Finance Wrap Closings
stages.detail: Horne Real Estate Law's reported incidence across its wrap closings.

stages.label: Subject-To Houses per Call
stages.detail: Pace Morby's estimate, including deals using land trusts; he adds a land trust does not stop the clause.

stages.label: Acceleration Cure Window
stages.conversion: Pay off, refinance, or deed back
stages.detail: In Rem Podcast found a 30-day window in every clause reviewed, with lenders usually offering a 30-day title-back option.

stages.label: Post-Reinstatement Wait
stages.conversion: No deed transfer before the wait clears
stages.detail: Morby waits 10 to 15 days after reinstatement to close escrow; a deed moved 3 days in is his most common cause of a call.

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before a Hybrid or Wrap Closes
diagrams.subtitle: Lien coverage, real arrears, active income, borrower pre-screen
diagrams.caption: Kill-or-proceed gates practitioners apply when structuring subject-to plus seller-note hybrids and carrying wrap paper.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is an organizing sequence; each rule is stated by the attributed practitioner, and the $5,000 buffer is Pace Morby's reported legal-fee gap.
diagrams.note: Sources: Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network (it6vSh38OhY), Pace Morby (t7aFESM6V_k, rQCg4GFRLAI), Fusion Notes (JAyoDBTIEIE).

nodes.question: Is the wrap balance at least equal to every underlying lien, including modification, down-payment assistance and 0% HUD liens?
nodes.fail_action: Restructure; the position can drift upside down (Scott Horne).

nodes.question: Are payoff and arrears confirmed with the lender, plus about $5,000 for legal fees?
nodes.fail_action: Rebuild the entry fee; the title company is not the bank (Pace Morby).

nodes.question: If using the Morby Method, is active income coming in on the deal?
nodes.fail_action: Kill the Morby Method; people take the cash out and bail (Pace Morby).

nodes.question: Does a five-minute pre-screen show no bankruptcies, foreclosures or missed mortgage payments in the last 12 months?
nodes.fail_action: Decline to carry paper on the wrap (Fusion Notes).

diagrams.title: From Bid to Partial Sale to First Position
diagrams.subtitle: Price it, audit it, size the partial, clean up the wrap
diagrams.caption: A four-stage path for buying a note, selling a front partial and keeping the tail, built from Paperstac and Cal Ewing operating rules.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week labels are an organizing frame; practitioners did not state a four-week timeline. Dollar and yield figures are their reported examples.

weeks.title: Lock an Indicative Bid
weeks.deliverable: Bid built off verified rate, UPB, origination date and last pay date

weeks.title: Clean the Collateral
weeks.deliverable: FBO wording, address and signer confirmed and screenshotted
weeks.gate: Vesting verified before collateral goes to the auditor (Paperstac)

weeks.title: Size and Model the Partial
weeks.deliverable: On a $400 payment, 12 months equals $4,800; paying $4,000 earns about 20% while $5,000 loses money
weeks.gate: Payoff, auction and REO splits modeled before any partial sells (Cal Ewing)

weeks.title: Move the Wrap to First Position
weeks.deliverable: Title run, underlying lien disclosed, partial proceeds pay it off
